business_scope.primary_industry_name: Manufacture of Absorbable Polyglycolic Acid Braided Sutures

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (Civil Law base with Anglo-American-inspired corporate statutes)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Panama–United States Trade Promotion Agreement (TPA), active investment chapter protections
Panama bilateral investment treaty programme with OECD and Latin American counterparts (various active BITs)
Territorial taxation regime; limited double-taxation agreements, supplemented by tax information exchange agreements

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law 23 of April 27, 2015 (AML/CFT framework, as amended), Executive Decree 363 of July 10, 2015, Law 62 of 2016, Law 70 of August 30, 2019 (Final Beneficial Owner Registry), implementing decisions of the Registro Público de Panamá, and FATF-aligned regulations applied by the Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF) and competent supervisory authorities.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Local issuance; no apostille required for Panama-origin registry certificate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: General Power of Attorney executed by each foreign subscriber/shareholder in favour of the Panama incorporation attorney
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public of the shareholder's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization for non-Hague countries) plus sworn Spanish translation before a Panama public translator

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / incumbency certificate for any corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent companies registry or statutory registrar of the corporate shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization for non-Hague countries) plus sworn Spanish translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board resolution of each corporate shareholder authorizing the subscription, purchase, or holding of Panama shares

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based screening against OFAC SDN, UN Security Council consolidated sanctions, EU/UK consolidated lists, Panama's national sanctions notifications, and UAF alerts at onboarding and before any share transfer. Enhanced due diligence is applied to all foreign and domestic PEPs, family members and close associates under Law 23 of 2015, including source-of-wealth verification, beneficial-owner tracing, and ongoing transaction monitoring. Suspicious transactions must be reported to the Unidad de Análisis Financiero without delay; failure to comply subjects the resident agent and entity to sanctions, fines, or dissolution.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá – Plataforma de Servicios en Línea / Sede Electrónica (https://www.registropublico.gob.pa)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be expressed in Latin script; Spanish is the official working language of the Registry. Foreign-origin names are accepted when transliterated phonetically into Spanish or English/Latin characters. The name must be distinguishable from any existing registered name and must not mislead as to corporate form; the name must contain or have the suffix 'Sociedad Anónima' or 'S.A.' unless otherwise authorized.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Name reservations are not extendable. If the name is refused, the applicant may file a 'recurso de reconsideración' before the Dirección General de Registro Público within five business days of notification, stating the basis for review and submitting evidence that the name is distinguishable. If reconsideration is denied, the applicant may pursue an administrative appeal under Panama's Administrative Procedure Law (Ley 38 de 2000) or simply file a new name reservation with a materially different designation. Registry determinations based on trademark or registered-business confusion may be cured by written authorization from the prior-name holder.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office and registered-agent services are permissible for corporate formality, but each Sociedad Anónima must maintain a resident agent with a physical street address in Panama. A virtual address cannot satisfy manufacturing, sanitary, or operational substance requirements; the suture-needle manufacturing/assembly activity will require a physical commercial establishment, prior sanitary registration with the Ministerio de Salud (MINSA), import/export registration, and pharmacotechnical oversight where applicable.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 65%–75% after operational commencement under a MINSA sanitary license for medical device manufacturing; 5%–10% if the entity is maintained solely as a non-operational shelf/holding vehicle during the pre-incorporation stage.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law 32 of 1927 on Corporations (Ley 32 de 1927 sobre Sociedades Anónimas), as amended; particularly Articles 1-5 (formation and name), Articles 6-9 (capital and shares), Article 54 (board and officers); supplemented by the General Registry Regulations under Resolution No. 212-2017 of the Registro Público de Panamá.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Sección Mercantil (Panama Public Registry, Mercantile Section)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Pacto Social (Articles of Incorporation) and Estatutos (Bylaws), executed by public deed (Escritura Pública) and presented for inscription
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; no escrow deposit required. At least one share must be subscribed; capital may be denominated in any currency (often USD) and paid in installments as set by the board within the Pacto Social
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Corporation, having received the subscriptions set forth in the Pacto Social, hereby ratifies the issuance and allotment of common shares to the founding subscriber; RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office of the Corporation is established at [City], Republic of Panama, and the maintenance of the legal and fiscal records at the registered agent's office is approved; RESOLVED FURTHER, that [Director A] is appointed President, [Director B] is appointed Secretary-Treasurer, and the President is authorized to execute all banking, licensing, and administrative instruments; RESOLVED FINALLY, that the officers are empowered to procure the sanitary registration, industrial license, and environmental permits required for the manufacture of surgical sutures.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Reservation and Drafting of Pacto Social
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá (Name Reservation) and designated Panamanian legal counsel
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit two alternative corporate names via the Quiosco del Registro Público or online portal; obtain the Certificado de Nombre (name availability certificate). Draft the Pacto Social and Estatutos stating corporate purpose, authorized capital, subscriber shares, registered agent, board particulars, and domicile.
required_dossiers: Passport copies of all subscribers, directors, and officers
Name reservation application with two alternative names
Consent letter of the registered agent (agente residente)
Draft Pacto Social and Estatutos
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for similarity or prohibited terms, refile with alternative names and obtain a fresh Certificado de Nombre; cure defects by amending the draft before notarization.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notaría Pública del Circuito de Panamá
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Appear before a Panamanian notary with the finalized draft; execute the public deed containing the Pacto Social, statutory articles, capital subscription, registered agent appointment, and initial directors; pay notarial fees and fiscal stamps.
required_dossiers: Final draft Escritura de Constitución
Valid passports of subscribers and directors
Certificado de Nombre
Registered agent appointment form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Require the notary to correct any discrepancy or irregular clause prior to signature; if pages are defective, re-execute the deed with proper attestation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inscription in the Panama Public Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Sección Mercantil
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the certified copy of the Escritura Pública with the Mercantile Section; pay the official registration fee, fiscal stamps, and the registry arancel; obtain the stamped inscription and the corporate Ficha de Persona Jurídica (corporate identification record).
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the notarized Escritura Pública
Original protocolized deed copy
Official fee payment receipt (bank deposit or web payment)
Fiscal stamp certificates (derechos de timbre)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues an objection (reparo), file an amended public deed addressing the cited clauses; remove or modify irregular provisions and re-present within the registry's statutory term.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration (RUC) at the Dirección General de Ingresos
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete Form FM-01 (Registro Único de Contribuyentes) and submit the registered corporate documents at DGI's nearest office or through the Sede Electrónica; receive the RUC certificate required for banking, importation of raw materials, and municipal licensing.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the registered Escritura Pública
Ficha de Persona Jurídica from the Public Registry
RUC application form FM-01
Registered agent and director identification documents
Apostilled certificate of incumbency (if foreign directors)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RUC application is rejected or questioned, supply the missing documentation, correct the applicant data, and re-present through DGI's digital platform; permanently resolving discrepancies before fines accrue.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Records, Board Resolution, and Share Certificates
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registered agent / corporate secretary with notarial support
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Notarize the pro-forma First Board Resolution; open the statutory corporate books (Libro de Actas de la Junta Directiva, Libro de Accionistas, Libro de Registro de Acciones); issue and deliver share certificates against subscriber payments; execute officer consent forms.
required_dossiers: Pro-forma First Board Resolution (board minutes)
Share subscription agreements
Director and officer consent to act (acceptance letters)
Share certificate stock and ledgers
Registered agent certification of books
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct omissions or irregular allotments by a ratifying board resolution; if share issuance is faulty, effect a transfer or reallocation under Law 32 and update the share ledger accordingly.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Operating Notice and Commercial License
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alcaldía de Panamá / Municipio del Corregimiento
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Aviso de Operación (operating notice) with the municipality of the industrial premises; declare the business classification, address, and equipment; pay the municipal patent fee and obtain the temporary operating permiso for the manufacturing site.
required_dossiers: RUC certificate
Certified copy of registered articles of incorporation
Lease agreement or title deed for the industrial premises
Fire safety clearance (initial municipal inspection form)
Municipal zoning/use of soil certification
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipal office raises zoning or classification objections, apply for a special industrial use permit, amend the premises description, or file a reconsideration motion before the Municipal Council within the prescribed period.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministerio de Salud (MINSA) — Dirección Nacional de Farmacia y Drogas (DNFD) for medical device sanitary registration; Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI) — Dirección Nacional de Empresas e Industrias for industrial operating authorization
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Registro Sanitario de Dispositivos Médicos (Medical Device Sanitary Registration) and Licencia Industrial / Aviso de Operación Industrial

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE) — Dirección de Normas y Evaluación de Impacto Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category II — Diagnóstico Ambiental de Bajo Impacto (low-impact environmental diagnosis / abbreviated EIA) for a sterile medical device assembly and packaging facility; a full EsIA (Category III) is generally not required unless significant VOC emissions or hazardous waste volumes exceed the thresholds.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharges must comply with Executive Decree No. 130 of 1997 (pH 6.5–8.5; total suspended solids ≤150 mg/L; biological oxygen demand ≤250 mg/L; heavy metals below the schedule of parameters). Air emissions and volatile organic compound (VOC) fugitive releases must meet Executive Decree No. 80 of 2011 ambient air quality standards; hazardous clinical/biological waste from suture manufacturing must be rendered non-infectious and disposed under Resolution AG-0191-2017 of MiAMBIENTE on hospital waste management.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification (Certificado de Seguridad, Prevención y Protección Contra Incendios) from the Benemérito Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá covering the cleanroom and storage areas; structural load inspection and seismic review of the assembly line mezzanine by an IIA-approved structural engineer; occupational health workplace clearance issued by the Dirección General de Salud Ocupacional (MINSA) confirming ventilation, sterility controls, and employee medical surveillance protocols.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas; portal: Sede Electrónica (https://dgi.mef.gob.pa)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1) Incorporate a Panamanian Sociedad Anónima (S.A.) or register a foreign company branch with the Public Registry; a resident agent (agente residente) is mandatory for non-resident entities. 2) Obtain a municipal business license (Aviso de Operación) from the Alcaldía of the place of operation. 3) Register with DGI using Formulario de Registro Único de Contribuyentes (RUC), submitting incorporation documents, municipal license, identity documents, and proof of local commercial address. 4) Upon approval, DGI issues the NIT/RUC and simultaneously activates the ITBMS (VAT) registration for taxable activities. A taxable representative may be required for foreign entities with no physical residence in Panama.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama does not provide a check-the-box election or hybrid mismatch election regimes. S.A. entities are automatically treated as taxable entities subject to territorial income tax on Panama-source income. Eligible small taxpayers may elect the simplified taxation regime (Régimen Simplificado) based on annual gross income, and taxpayers may elect consolidated filing for VAT and income tax under DGI procedures. No CFC or hybrid entity classifications are available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS (Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios) – VAT equivalent
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: B/. 0 – no statutory economic threshold; any person or entity engaging in taxable imports, transfer of movable goods, or services during the ordinary course of business must register for ITBMS with DGI prior to commencing operations. Small taxpayers with annual gross income below B/. 36,000 may be eligible for simplified accounting and filing obligations.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Panama mandates electronic invoicing (Facturación Electrónica) for all ITBMS-registered taxpayers through DGI-certified software or the Sede Electrónica platform. Invoices must be transmitted in XML format in real time or within 24 hours (for large taxpayers via API integration) to DGI for fiscal clearance and digital stamping (Firma Digital). The system authenticates invoices and credit documents (Comprobantes de Crédito Fiscal); failure to obtain clearance blocks issuance of valid invoices.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods physically exported from Panama through customs exit (as evidenced by the customs export declaration) qualify for the 0% ITBMS rate. Services rendered to non-residents for use outside Panama and export-related services provided to international shipping/aircraft (e.g., freight, bunkering, repair, dockside services) may also qualify for zero-rating. The taxpayer must be an ITBMS registrant, maintain transactional records, and substantiate foreign exchange repatriation when applicable. Excess input VAT on export operations may be claimed as a refund (saldo a favor) through quarterly or annual refund filing.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DUA / Declaración Única Aduanera)
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill (B/L or AWB)
FOB Value Evidence and Inward Remittance Certificate (Certificado de Reintegro de Divisas)
Certificate of Origin or National Production Certificate (when claiming preferential treatment)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGI conducts targeted fiscal audits on zero-rated export claims, requiring full documentary proof of physical export and foreign payment collection. For fraudulent zero-rating claims, DGI retroactively claws back the full ITBMS at 7% plus 10% late surcharge and monthly interest, and imposes fines of 25% to 100% of the omitted tax depending on degree of intent. Criminal tax fraud penalties under the Código Fiscal and Decree Law 2/2020 may involve imprisonment of 2 to 5 years; the prescription period extends to 10 years in cases of fraud, preventing statute-of-limitations defenses.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) — the Republic of Panama is fully dollarized and maintains no central bank; prudential bank supervision rests with the SBP, while monetary conditions are de facto determined by the U.S. Federal Reserve. The Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF) manages fiscal policy but exercises no foreign-exchange control authority.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Complete convertibility under a dual-currency regime: the U.S. dollar is unlimited legal tender and the Panamanian balboa (PAB) is a nominal unit pegged 1:1 to the USD (only fractional coins circulate). Capital and current account transactions are freely convertible with no exchange-control license, repatriation approval, or quantitative limits. Profit remittance friction is exclusively fiscal: DGI (Dirección General de Ingresos) requires the filing of the dividend declaration and payment of the 10% dividend withholding tax (5% for taxable income under USD 1.5 million) before external transfer; no SBP clearance is required.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable — Panama imposes no surrender, conversion, or repatriation timeline on export proceeds. The manufacturing S.A. may lawfully retain 100% of USD receipts (or any other currency) in domestic or foreign bank accounts; no mandatory conversion ratio exists because the USD is the domestic currency.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational USD Account (primary) + Capital Escrow Account for shareholder equity injection
Operational Account with committed Commercial LC/Import Letter of Credit Lines (MT700)
Trade Finance Account — dedicated USD collection, documentary credit, and LC disbursement rail
Operational Account (state-owned; requires demonstrable domestic payroll and DGI records)
Corporate Global USD Account with notional pooling through Citi New York nostro

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low as a primary banking substitute and Medium as a supplementary disbursement rail. Panama has no domestic EMI (Electronic Money Institution) licensing category; the SBP prohibits unlicensed deposit acceptance and all final USD settlement must transit a Panama-licensed bank's U.S. correspondent. Offshore EMIs and regional fintechs may be used only as pre-funded cards or virtual accounts for small operational expenses; LC issuance, trade settlement, and regulatory compliance must remain with a licensed Tier-1 bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: SBP Rule 2-2015 does not statutorily mandate physical appearance, but onboarding practice at Tier-1 banks requires one of two paths: (i) physical attendance of at least one signatory and the beneficial owner at a Panama branch, or (ii) remote opening with the director executing powers before a Panama Notary Public, apostilled corporate documents, and a compliance video-interview with the Panamanian Resident Agent. A purely remote opening with zero Panama nexus is a Low-probability outcome for a newly formed S.A.; the recommended path is a 2-day director visit or delegation to a Panamanian officer-agent with banking powers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Lapsed or absent Declaración de Beneficiario Final (beneficial ownership filing) at the Registro Público (Law 23/2015, Order 190-2019, Law 129/2020); look-through required where a Private Interest Foundation (PIF) is shareholder
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified recent registry certificate evidencing the DBF submission; sworn BO statement naming the ultimate natural person; PIF foundation charter and council resolution identifying foundation beneficiaries; foundation accounting records.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Legalization gap: foreign incorporator/shareholder documents without apostille or certified Spanish translation; inability to match original certificates
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Hague Apostille on all foreign birth and company records; sworn translation by a Panamanian Public Translator; legalized copy of the S.A. public deed (Escritura) and constitutional resolution; original registered share register and share certificates.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Business activity and economic substance mismatch — medical-device manufacturing claimed but no tax or sanitary licenses in the KYC file
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: DGI RUC certificate; MINSA medical-device manufacturing permit (Registro Sanitario); municipal Aviso de Operación; audited or reviewed financial statements; purchase orders and distribution contracts for surgical sutures; plant lease or property title.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, PEP, or adverse-media flags on non-resident shareholders or counterparties
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent OFAC/EU/SBP sanctions screening; negative PEP declarations; sworn source-of-wealth letters for injections above USD 1 million; originator bank statements and MT103 history showing trade-linked funds; corporate CV of material shareholders.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unverifiable initial capital — funds arriving in crypto, bearer instruments, or from jurisdictionally high-risk bank accounts
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Shareholder capital-subscription minutes; written confirmation from the originator bank; commercial purpose mapping to the acquisition of PGA braided-suture machinery and needle steel; transferor tax returns; express refusal to accept crypto-funded contributions.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route USD equity from the foreign shareholder/PIF via SWIFT MT103 or Fedwire into a dedicated 60-90 day Capital Escrow Account at Banco General, referencing 'Aporte de Capital – PA_CORP, RUC {identifier}' with the beneficiary name matching the S.A. exactly. No SBP authorization or balance-of-payments registration is required; the bank books the credit as capital/liability and DGI compliance is satisfied through the annual sworn tax return. To avoid reclassification as shareholder loans, execute a notarized capital-subscription resolution and record it at the Registro Público; then sweep the escrow to the operational account, attaching the bank attestation to the source-of-funds file.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Supplier settlements use (i) SWIFT MT103 telegraphic transfers for prepayments and low-value raw-material invoices, (ii) irrevocable Commercial Letters of Credit (at-sight or 90-day usance) opened via Banistmo or Banco General with MT700/MT710 confirmation for needle steel and PGA polymer components, and (iii) documentary collections (URC 522) for repeat suppliers. Because Panama has no central bank and no domestic Fedwire/CHIPS node, all USD is finally settled through each bank's U.S. correspondent (New York nostro), so MT103 cut-off times and correspondent charges must be pre-agreed; LC documents must include MINSA Registro Sanitario and certificate of origin for medical-device components to avoid discrepancies.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: USD/EUR outright deliverable forwards contracted with licensed Panamanian banks or U.S. counterparties (margined on the U.S. nostro)
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on restricted or exotic pairs — CNY, KRW, INR — to hedge raw-material sourcing from Asian suppliers without physical delivery
USD-based cross-currency swaps (XCCY) converting EUR or JPY procurement liabilities into USD-linked floating flows
Vanilla FX put/call options on USD crosses (e.g., EUR/USD) for budget certainty on European needle and packaging imports

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporation Franchise Tax (Impuesto Anual de la Sociedad)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance, Panama
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due by 30 April of each calendar year for the preceding corporate fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Statutory interest and monthly surcharge accrue from 1 May; the entity loses good standing with DGI; non-payment for two consecutive years may trigger administrative strike-off by the Registro Público.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Registry Report (Informe Anual de la Sociedad)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filing window is 1 January through 31 March of each year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Registry good standing is blocked; certification and transactional filings are suspended; repeated and prolonged non-filing may result in administrative cancellation of the corporate inscription.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A private Panama Sociedad Anónima is not generally required to appoint external auditors or file audited financial statements. Independent audit is compulsory for entities regulated by the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (banks and trust companies), the Superintendencia del Mercado de Valores (listed issuers), and the Superintendencia de Seguros y Reaseguros (insurers); a parent company or lender may also contractually require an audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Private S.A. entities maintain statutory books and tax records under generally accepted accounting principles in Panama (local GAAP-PCGA) when not otherwise regulated; banks and public-interest entities are required to apply IFRS as issued by the IASB where directed by their prudential regulator.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Panama does not operate a public annual UBO filing register for the standard S.A. Under Law 23 of 2015, the resident agent is required to keep a private beneficial ownership record and annually refresh its client due diligence and ownership schedule. Share transfers must be pushed into the Register of Members via endorsed share certificates, and the updated beneficial ownership details must be supplied to the resident agent after each transfer; no Registry filing of the UBO schedule is required.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 400–1,200 per annum depending on registered-agent service level and domiciliation address
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500–6,500 per engagement for a private manufacturing S.A. when an audit is required by a parent company, lender, or investor

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (graduated three-tier system: 15% on net taxable income up to B/.50,000; 20% on income between B/.50,001 and B/.1,500,000; 25% on income exceeding B/.1,500,000)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general corporate tax holiday or investment allowance exists in the general territorial regime. Export-oriented exemptions may apply only under specific licensed regimes (e.g., Colon Free Zone, Panama Pacifico, SEM/Multinational HQ), none of which are presumed for a standard S.A. engaged in surgical suture assembly. A minimum tax floor of 4.17% of gross taxable income applies under Article 699-B of the Fiscal Code when it exceeds the regular ISR computation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 120 (Declaración Jurada de Impuesto sobre la Renta – Personas Jurídicas); filed electronically via the DGI e-Tax 2.0 portal (https://etax.dgi.gob.pa) with payment processed through the T@ Pagas system. Quarterly advance ISR payments are compulsory for taxpayers whose prior-year tax exceeded B/.50,000.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual return with mandatory quarterly advance payments (April 15, July 15, October 15, and December 15 of the tax year, or as notified by the DGI).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within three months after the close of the calendar tax year; for a 31 December year-end the return must be filed by 31 March of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Unique taxpayer identification number (Registro Único de Contribuyente).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident S.A. without a permanent establishment must be registered through its Panamanian resident agent (agente residente), who holds the power of attorney and must certify the entity's active status.
The taxable year for a non-resident S.A. is the calendar year; deviations require prior DGI authorization and are rarely granted.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Primary economic activity code, e.g., ISIC 3250 – manufacture of medical and surgical instruments and supplies.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declare the precise local activity producing Panama-source revenue; foreign-source export sales of assembled sutures are not Panama-source under the territorial rule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Panama-source gross revenue from domestic sales of surgical sutures and needle assemblies.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only revenue derived from activities carried out in Panama is included; revenue from offshore customers without Panamanian source is excluded and must be reconciled in the notes to the return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible manufacturing costs (raw materials, direct labor, plant overhead) supported by invoices, contracts, and bank records.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductions are allowed only when the expenditure is real, documented, and causally linked to Panama-source income; related-party costs must comply with Law 7 of 2015 transfer pricing rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income after statutory deductions, depreciation, and allowed tax-loss carryforward (maximum five years).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the non-resident operates through a permanent establishment, profit must be allocated using the separate-accounts method; a portion equal to a profit margin acceptable to the DGI must remain taxable in Panama.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computed ISR using the graduated 15%/20%/25% schedule.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the same graduated schedule; the 4.17% minimum tax floor may override the result where gross income is proportionally high.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credits for quarterly advance payments, third-party withholdings, and any prior-year surplus; final balance due or refund requested.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach a reconciliation of all advance credits; refunds are subject to DGI audit and the three-year statutory refund period.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a surcharge of 10% of the tax due for the first month and 1% per additional month, capped at 30%, plus default interest of 1% per month (approximately 12.68% effective annually). The DGI may additionally impose a fixed fine of B/.100 to B/.1,000 per unfiled return and suspend the RUC until compliance.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% withholding on dividends paid out of Panama-source profits (Article 733 of the Fiscal Code, as amended by Law 28 of 2010). The rate increases to 20% when the beneficial owner is deemed resident in a preferentially low-tax jurisdiction (tax haven) under Panama's blacklist rules. Dividends paid from profits already subject to the complementary corporate-level tax or from foreign-source income are not subject to this levy.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Panama's DTA network is limited (in force with Mexico, Korea, Singapore, Barbados, Qatar, and UAE, plus limited shipping/air agreements). To invoke relief, the beneficial owner must submit to the withholding agent prior to the payment date: (i) a Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) issued by the home tax authority for the calendar year of payment; (ii) a sworn declaration of ultimate beneficial ownership and economic substance; and (iii) any specific DGI form applicable to the treaty. The withholding agent must obtain DGI validation before applying the reduced rate; if withholding was excessive, a refund claim must be filed with the DGI within the three-year statutory refund period.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest: 12.5% statutory rate for cross-border interest paid to non-residents where the loaned funds are used in Panama; reduced to 10% under the Mexico, Korea, Singapore, and UAE DTAs. Royalties: 12.5% statutory rate for payments for the use of intangibles in Panama; treaty rate generally capped at 10%. Payments for technical services related to manufacturing may be recharacterized as royalties where substance tests are not met.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: B/.300,000 (USD 300,000) of aggregate related-party cross-border transactions per fiscal year triggers mandatory Transfer Pricing documentation (Local File) and the annual informational return Form 230. A Master File is required where the multinational group's consolidated annual turnover exceeds B/.5 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama does not maintain a standalone Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) filing for ordinary S.A. entities, but applies substance-based anti-abuse rules under Law 52 of 2016 and Decree 740 of 2016 (Regime of International Tax Transparency). A manufacturing S.A. must demonstrate in Panama: physical plant premises, qualified operational employees, inventory, board meetings and executive decisions, and bank accounts. The DGI may recharacterize offshore-booked income as Panama-source if the assembly, warehousing, management, or revenue-generating activity occurs within Panamanian territory. Licensed entities under SEM (multinational HQ), Colon Free Zone, or Panama Pacifico are subject to formal economic substance reporting and payroll/physical-asset thresholds.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful omission of Panama-source revenue, fraudulent invoicing, false deductions, or the routing of local surgical suture sales through an offshore related distributor lacking real economic substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative: 50% fraud surcharge on the omitted tax plus monthly default interest and the reversal of all related deductions. Criminal: under Law 8 of 2010 and the Penal Code, imprisonment of two to five years and a fine equivalent to the amount of tax evaded; aggravating circumstances apply when false documents are used.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors signing or approving a false return are jointly and severally liable for the omitted tax and penalties. The DGI may impose precautionary asset freezes, publish the taxpayer on the official delinquent-debtor list, impose travel bans, and pursue criminal indictment resulting in imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintenance of an S.A. without physical premises, personnel, or operational activity; use of a nominee agent as a letterbox while manufacturing, inventory, or revenue generation occurs in Panama but profits are booked offshore.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DGI recharacterization of foreign income as Panama-source, retroactive assessment for up to five years, application of a 50% surcharge and default interest, and cancellation of the RUC. Repeated non-compliance may lead to strike-off of the corporation under Law 32 of 1927 and loss of the benefit of limited liability.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Nominee directors and registered agents may face administrative fines and suspension of their licenses. Actual directors risk joint liability for re-assessed taxes and, in egregious laundering scenarios, criminal prosecution and travel restrictions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Receiving substantial cash payments for surgical consumables without customer due diligence, concealing the beneficial owner of the S.A., or utilizing personal accounts to settle commercial invoices in breach of Law 23 of 2015 and the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) framework.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Corporate fines up to B/.1,000,000 per infraction, asset forfeiture, suspension of operations, and cancellation of commercial registrations. Directors and compliance officers face personal fines of B/.50,000 to B/.500,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly accept illicit funds or conceal the true beneficial owner are exposed to criminal money-laundering charges under Articles 254–260 of the Penal Code, carrying imprisonment of five to ten years, bank-account freezes, and travel bans.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Cross-border related-party transactions exceeding B/.300,000 without preparation of the Local File / Master File or failure to file Form 230 with the annual return; or pricing of intercompany suture component purchases inconsistently with the arm's-length standard.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: A fine of 1% of the aggregate value of the relevant related-party transactions (minimum B/.10,000), plus an arm's-length adjustment adding the difference to the taxable base, with applicable default interest and surcharges.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who certify false transfer pricing documentation are jointly liable for the resulting tax adjustment and fines; the DGI may also report the matter to the Public Prosecutor's Office where fraudulent documentation is identified.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distribution of dividends to foreign shareholders without withholding and remitting the 10% (or 20% for blacklist-jurisdiction recipients) dividend tax, including disguised distributions through shareholder loan waivers or constructive dividends.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The withholding agent (the S.A.) is personally liable for the un-withheld tax under Article 733-A of the Fiscal Code, plus a 50% surcharge and monthly default interest; the payment may also be disallowed as an expense.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who authorized distributions knowing that the withholding was not remitted are jointly and severally liable for the tax and penalties, and may be subject to travel bans and criminal prosecution for misappropriation of tax funds.
